definitions.explanation: The humble or formal term for one's own grandmother. Used when speaking about your grandmother to others in polite contexts.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{元気|げんき}です。
{祖母|そぼ}は{今年|ことし}{八十歳|はちじゅっさい}になります。
examples.english: My grandmother will turn 80 this year.

examples.japanese: {毎週|まいしゅう}{祖母|そぼ}に{電話|でんわ}します。
examples.english: I call my grandmother every week.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}は{遠|とお}くに{住|す}んでいますので、{夏休|なつやす}みによく{会|あ}いに{行|い}きます。
examples.english: My grandmother lives far away, so I often go to see her during summer vacation.

examples.japanese: {私|わたし}の{祖母|そぼ}は{若|わか}い{時|とき}、{先生|せんせい}でした。{今|いま}でも{本|ほん}を{読|よ}むのが{好|す}きです。
examples.english: My grandmother was a teacher when she was young. She still likes reading books.

notes:
{祖母|そぼ} is the humble/formal term for one's own grandmother, used when speaking to others in polite or formal contexts.

FAMILY TERM REGISTER:
- {祖母|そぼ}: humble/formal (about your own grandmother)
- おばあさん: neutral-polite (about someone else's grandmother)
- おばあちゃん: casual/affectionate (direct address or about your own)
- おばあさま: respectful (about someone else's grandmother)

COMPANION TERMS:
- {祖父|そふ}: grandfather (same humble/formal register)
- {祖父母|そふぼ}: grandparents

USAGE:
In writing, essays, and formal speech, {祖母|そぼ} is standard. In everyday conversation, most people say おばあちゃん when talking about their own grandmother.

NOTE:
{外祖母|がいそぼ} specifically means maternal grandmother, and {内祖母|ないそぼ} means paternal grandmother, but these terms are rarely used in daily conversation.
